attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter, presented as his assessment of Nebius's shareholder letter.

semantics.note: The claim is an unhedged present-tense observation that the 300MW New Jersey build is going badly. The normalisation captures it; the March 2025 start date is background.

contract.note: Zitron named no measure. Reading 'going badly' as substantial delays or construction problems is fair and ordinary. Anchoring to Q4 2025, the period his cited letter covers, is reasonable. Both conditions require a milestone comparison.

evidence.note: In the Q4 2025 call, management says the first Microsoft tranche was delivered on time and the rest is on track. This weighs against the claim, but it is a company statement about itself and does not compare construction milestones.
The annual filing confirms the first tranche was delivered in November 2025, inside the target quarter. It does not say whether that was on schedule or how the campus build compares with plan.

reviews.rationale: Neither condition is met. Nothing in the packet shows missed milestones or serious obstacles in Q4 2025. Against the claim there is only management's word that the first tranche was on time, plus a filing that dates it to November. The contract says one on-time tranche does not show the whole build was on schedule. No comparison of planned and achieved construction milestones exists, so the evidence does not settle it.
